_note: COLLECTIVE EDGE HAS NO COLOR OF ITS OWN. Black, white, and a grey ramp, and that palette is not going to grow. There is no CE gold, no CE accent. That is not the same as saying a CE surface is always grey: CE almost never appears alone, and on a co-brand surface the color is the PARTNER's. The rule that holds both facts is 'CE stays monochrome, the color belongs to the partner.' Color appears in four places, none of them a CE hue. (1) The Edge wedge in the block mark, grey #C8C8C8 when CE stands alone and the partner's color on a co-brand surface (see the top-level 'wedge' block). (2) On a partner-led co-brand surface the partner's palette leads and CE adds no hue. (3) On a CE-led product for a partner or their customer, the partner's accent is the one hue, used functionally (active nav, live state, one chart series). (4) Charts pick series colors for legibility and colorblind separation, not from this palette. White is the primary surface for documents; black is reserved for hero, section-divider and title surfaces. See SKILL.md section 2 for the co-brand rules.

black.role: Primary brand black; hero / divider surfaces

fog.role: The Edge wedge when CE stands alone. On a co-brand surface the wedge takes the partner's color instead; see the top-level wedge block

white.role: Primary brand white; primary document canvas

wedge._note: The Edge wedge is the ONE part of the block mark that carries color, and that color is the PARTNER's. CE has no hue of its own, so when CE co-brands it takes the partner's into its own mark; the partner enters through the wedge and nothing else moves. Block and letters stay black or white always. Every combination ships as a file (assets/logos/mark-on-{light,dark}-{grey,royal,apex}.svg), so never hand-recolor. As CE takes on more operating companies, each gets a wedge color here and nothing else changes.

standalone.role: CE standing alone. The default, and the only treatment on a CE-only surface. Note it nearly disappears at favicon sizes on a white tile; give the mark a dark backing rather than inventing a CE hue

byPartner._note: On a surface co-branded with that partner. Values are the partner kit's own primary, so they stay in step with that brand.

apex.role: Apex Paramedics gold, Pantone 1235 C, from apex-brand-kit

status._note: Used sparingly and functionally, healthcare context. Never decorative accents, and always paired with text or an arrow so meaning does not ride on color alone.

partners._note: 'Powered by Collective Edge' co-brand accents. THIS IS A CONVENIENCE MIRROR AND IT GOES STALE. Each partner's own brand kit is the source of truth for its colors and logos; pull from there. A partner's color may run the whole surface (partner-led mode A) or act as the single functional accent on a CE surface (CE-led mode B). It never colors the CE block or its letters. It DOES color the Edge wedge, which is the co-brand mechanism; see the top-level wedge block.
partners._textSafe: Bright partner brand colors usually fail 3:1 on white as text, small labels, or thin chart lines. Use the darkened step the partner's own kit ships (Apex gold #f9ad16 -> #B77808). Never invent your own darkening.

primary.role: Apex blue. The primary brand color: wordmark, headers, links, buttons

deep.role: Hero backgrounds, header bands, sidebars, section dividers, footers

gold.role: Signature accent. The arc, accent bars, kickers, stat numerals

goldDeep.role: Text-safe gold. Use for small or bold labels, icons, and thin chart lines on white; the bright gold fails contrast there

primary.role: Royal purple. Column headers, accent bars, contact labels, category badges

deep.role: Primary headers, hero backgrounds, section dividers

logoFill.role: Logo fill color, alternate dark accent

_unverified._note: No brand kit exists for these yet, so these hexes are inherited from the original design export and have NOT been reconciled against a source of truth. Confirm with the partner before shipping, and publish a kit when one of them becomes real work.
